subject: Banking
title: Mortgage-Backed Securities Fraud
description: A 60-second lesson on Mortgage-Backed Securities Fraud.

hook.text: Banks sold $2 trillion in toxic mortgage securities rated AAA. They knew the mortgages were bad. They sold them anyway.

buildup.text: Banks bundled subprime mortgages into securities and paid rating agencies to stamp them AAA.

discovery.text: Goldman Sachs created a product called Abacus, designed to fail, then bet against it.

twist.text: The fraud collapsed the global economy. 8.7 million jobs lost. $11 trillion in household wealth vanished.

climax.text: Mortgage fraud was the biggest financial scandal in history.

punchline.text: $11 trillion in losses. Banks knew. No one imprisoned. The system failed.

quiz.question: What did Goldman Sachs do with its Abacus product?
options: Sold it to clients while secretly betting it would fail
